title.narrative: ABA Promote the Rule of Law in Libya

description.narrative: ABA Promote the Rule of Law in Libya

General question: Results related to the intended outcome 2017Question: Summarise results related to the intended outcome (this information will be sent to Open Aid)Answer: The ABA continued to work within the legal sector to improve both legal education and the status of women via its intervention. The challenges were great, as the security situation has steadily worsened since fighting broke out in the capital, Tripoli in July 2014. Civil unrest and growing extremism have created widespread violence across the country that has prevented access to a large portion of the country; in particular access to Eastern Libya has been all but impossible. Cooperation with staff inside and outside the country has ensured that activities remain and that the programme remains alive. Activities continued to be conducted inside and outside the country, with study tours and workshops being held in Jordan, Tunisia and Turkey to help convene the target groups for implementation. Whilst there has been complete impediment to the work directly within the justice sector and in particular the training of prosecutors within districts across the country, working groups and study tours promoting the status of women both inside and outside the profession have proven very fruitful.
The intended outcome of the project continued to be the enhancement capacity of the legal profession in Libya, engaging both state and non-state actors to enhance the role of women, in society and within the profession itself.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
